identity.title: Decompose, Analyze and Rethink: Solving Intricate Problems with Human-like Reasoning Cycle

problem.claim: The paper addresses solving intricate problems with iterative reasoning inside a single large language model.

contributions.claim: Introduces DeAR, which builds a reasoning tree through Decompose, Analyze, and Rethink stages.
Uses tree-based question decomposition and globally updates rationales through natural-language feedback at each reasoning step.
Reports improved accuracy, fewer logical errors, and a better accuracy–reasoning-time trade-off than ToT and GoT across evaluated settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish DeAR from rationale-extension and search-based methods by combining tree-based question decomposition with global rationale updating.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on ScienceQA, StrategyQA, and GSM8K across various LLMs, with reduced logical errors and enhanced performance.
The authors report that DeAR achieves a superior trade-off between accuracy and reasoning time compared with Tree-of-Thoughts and Graph-of-Thoughts.

narrative_sequence.summary: DeAR is presented as an iterative reasoning-tree framework for intricate problems within one LLM.
Its planning uses tree-based question decomposition and global natural-language feedback to update rationales.
Decompose creates sub-question nodes, Analyze generates and self-checks node rationales, and Rethink updates parent rationales from child feedback.
The authors position the global update process as enabling adaptive structures and timely error correction relative to ToT and GoT.
Experiments are reported on three reasoning benchmarks, including an accuracy–reasoning-time comparison with ToT and GoT.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps named reasoning stages to concrete state changes: adding sub-question nodes, checking local rationales, and revising parent rationales from child feedback.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the mechanism easier to connect to the claimed error-correction behavior.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-stage reasoning method, specify each stage's input, persistent state, update operation, and information flow.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the method has no iterative state or hierarchical dependencies.

unknowns: The abstract gives no benchmark scores, baselines beyond ToT and GoT, model identities, statistical details, or definitions of logical error and reasoning time.
The claimed superiority and causal link between global updating and error correction are author-reported and not independently verified here.
